after: ## Where Section B sits on Route B
alt: Paper 2b split into Section A on the anthology and Section B on the unseen poem, 30 marks and about 45 minutes each. Section B comes second, so time must be protected, and comparison skills from Section A transfer.
caption: Protect a full 45 minutes for the unseen poem.

alt: A grid of the four lenses named in the specification, content, theme, structure and use of language, each with the question to ask and what it gives the answer. Structure is highlighted as the lens most often missed.
caption: Content, theme, structure, language: and never skip structure.

alt: Five strategies for a difficult unseen poem: work from what is clear, infer unfamiliar words or write about their effect, rearrange older word order, offer two possible speakers, and weigh two readings of an ambiguous ending.
caption: Start from what is clear and treat uncertainty as interpretation.

alt: The guide’s original poem Night Shift traced through its three stanzas: evening, when the mother leaves and her slippers point in; night, when hospital and child both keep watch; and morning, when the house at last lets go.
caption: The three stanzas move from leaving, to waiting, to release.

alt: The guide’s competent and stronger paragraphs on Night Shift compared: the stronger one opens with an argument, analyses the verb, image and line break, explains a precise effect and uses tentative, personal phrasing.
caption: Argue, analyse the exact method, explain the precise effect.

alt: A 45-minute bar and five steps for the unseen poem: read for sense (3 minutes), apply the four lenses (6), write a one-sentence argument (2), order three or four points ending with the ending (2), and write for about 30 minutes before checking.
caption: Thirteen minutes of thinking make thirty minutes of writing focused.
